Subject: Questions on chain-of-title + training restrictions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement/legal at LumenAI raised a couple of sticking points in the draft order form / SOW we wanted to clarify before we route back to our execs:

1) Chain of title: the SOW currently reads that LumenAI "owns output" produced by the service. We need written confirmation that that ownership is exclusive for our productization use (including sublicensing to our customers) and that Redwood will not assert ownership or claim derivative rights.

2) Training/data use: LumenAI has a strict internal policy about models being trained on our customer data. We need an explicit opt-out that prevents Redwood from using any LumenAI-provided data or outputs to train or improve Redwood models, and confirmation on what telemetry (if any) Redwood will retain.

3) Feedback & eval license: Your team asked for a feedback license in previous drafts. Procurement wants to limit that to anonymized, aggregate system telemetry for safety only, no productization.

Attached: BrightCo_SOW_v3.docx (our annotated copy) — we've highlighted suggested edits. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these constraints or propose language we can take to counsel?

Appreciate a quick read — if it's easier to sync, procurement can do a short call tomorrow.

Best,
Sophie

Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the annotated SOW. Looping in Legal (Olga) and Contracts (Karthik) to weigh in on precise phrasing. A few quick operational clarifications from product/sales side while legal reviews: 

- On output ownership: Redwood's standard position is that customers retain ownership of outputs they submit and receive. We typically avoid language that assigns "exclusive assignment" across downstream sublicensing without seeing the use-cases. If LumenAI needs explicit exclusive assignment for productization, we need to understand the scope (end-customer sublicensing? marketplace listing?) so we can map appropriate guardrails.

- On training opt-out: we can offer a contractual opt-out that prevents Redwood from using LumenAI data/outputs for model training. There are two patterns we recommend:
  * Per-account training opt-out (permanent) — adds operational overhead and affects model improvement across the fleet.
  * Scoped opt-out (timebox / environment): e.g., opt-out for production outputs for 12 months, but allow anonymized safety telemetry.

- Telemetry: we collect a handful of telemetry signals (latency, error rates, token counts, anonymized usage categories). We can agree to an evidence-only telemetry subset for debugging and safety with strict retention limits.

Immediate ask for legal: Olga/Karthik — can you propose redline language that: 1) preserves customer's right to use and sublicense outputs for productization; 2) gives LumenAI a binding training opt-out option (operationalized in Exhibit A); 3) limits Redwood's feedback license to anonymized/aggregate telemetry for safety and quality, with retention and deletion windows. Also advise on fallback language: if Redwood experiences capacity/compatibility issues we may propose routing to a functionally-equivalent 'fallback model' — we should document allowed fallback variants and obligations to notify.

Proposed next steps:
- Olga/Karthik redline and return by EOD tomorrow
- If redlines look reasonable, schedule a 30-min contract handoff call with LumenAI procurement (Sophie) and our CSM/Infra lead to confirm operational gating.

Thanks —
Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Sophie — thanks, I reviewed the annotated SOW and drafted a targeted redline set (attached: redlines_redwood_msa.docx). Summary of our recommended positions below so Procurement can evaluate trade-offs quickly: 

1) Output ownership / chain-of-title
- Proposal: Contract language stating: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Outputs created solely from Customer Data. Redwood grants no ownership interest in Customer Outputs."
- We add a narrow clarification to preserve Redwood's ability to provide and operate the service (e.g., logs, backups), but we explicitly exclude any assignment of derivative rights to Redwood.

2) Training & telemetry opt-out
- Proposal: Add Exhibit A (attached draft: proposed_exhibitA_training_optout.pdf) which gives Customer the right to opt-out of enabling any use of Customer Data or Customer Outputs for model training or improvement. The opt-out is implemented as a flag on the account and is effective immediately upon signature.
- Telemetry carve: we permit Redwood to retain anonymized safety telemetry (error rates, crash stack traces, coarse usage categories) strictly for debugging and security. All telemetry retained under this carve will be aggregated and retained for no longer than 90 days, unless otherwise mutually agreed.

3) Feedback license & productization
- Proposal: Limit the feedback license to "anonymized, aggregated telemetry necessary for monitoring, safety and troubleshooting." We explicitly prohibit use of Customer Outputs to improve commercial model weights or to create derivative models without additional written consent.

4) Fallback & routing language (operational)
- If Redwood routes requests to a fallback model variant due to capacity or compatibility, Redwood must: 1) notify Customer within 24 hours of first occurrence, 2) provide a compatibility matrix of the fallback variant (model family, approximate latency and expected cost delta), and 3) continue to enforce the Customer's training opt-out with the fallback variant.

Open questions for LumenAI to confirm:
- Do you require exclusive assignment (instead of a license) for Customer Outputs? We prefer a license/assignment-lite approach but can entertain assignment with additional commercial terms.
- Does Procurement require data residency-specific retention windows for telemetry longer than 90 days?

I've attached the redline. If these positions are acceptable, Karthik and I can mark them as our recommended baseline and we can prepare final MSA + Exhibit A for signature.

Olga Petrov
